block.prompt:
SPEAKING — a short talk (about 1–2 minutes).

Choose ONE of these angles on a cashless society:
(A) Cash, cards and PRIVACY — who can see what you buy?
(B) Going cashless and OLDER people or people without a bank account.
(C) Going cashless and SMALL businesses — card fees and machines that fail.

Prepare and then give a short talk that has: one clear main point, TWO details that support it, and ONE concrete example. Use the outline lines below only for brief notes — do NOT write out full sentences; you are going to SPEAK.
block.answer_key: A strong talk foregrounds ONE main point and orders the supporting detail clearly. Model outlines: (A) Main point: a cashless world makes every purchase traceable. Detail 1: banks/companies can build a profile of your habits. Detail 2: cash is the last fully anonymous option. Example: someone buying a private gift or a sensitive item. (B) Main point: going cashless can exclude people. Detail 1: not everyone has a smartphone or a bank account. Detail 2: some older people distrust or struggle with the technology. Example: a pensioner turned away from a cash-only-refusing café. (C) Main point: cashless payment quietly costs small shops money. Detail 1: card providers charge a fee on every sale. Detail 2: if the terminal or internet fails, the shop cannot sell at all. Example: a market stall losing a whole morning of trade in an outage. Assess structure, highlighting of the key point and supporting detail — not the position chosen.
block.acceptable_reasoning: Alle drei Blickwinkel sind gleichwertig; bewertet werden Struktur (ein Kernpunkt hervorgehoben, zwei stützende Details, ein Beispiel), Klarheit und zusammenhängendes Sprechen — nicht die Meinung.

levels: One main point clearly highlighted; two supporting details and an example in a logical order
Point present but detail loosely organised
No clear main point; ideas listed at random
Fluent, linked delivery with signposting (‚first', ‚for example', ‚so')
Good range of vocabulary and structures; errors rare
Adequate range; errors do not block meaning

watch_outs: Der häufigste Strukturfehler: alles gleich wichtig, kein hervorgehobener Kernpunkt. Vorab an einem Beispiel zeigen, wie man EINEN Punkt betont.
Vom Blatt ablesen unterbindet das freie Sprechen — nur Stichworte erlauben (deshalb bewusst nur wenige Notizzeilen).
‚Analyze' heißt hier: einen Aspekt herausgreifen und durchdringen, nicht das ganze Thema oberflächlich streifen.

subject: Lebende Fremdsprache
kompetenzbereich: An Gesprächen teilnehmen und zusammenhängendes Sprechen
